steps: Fill the stockpot with water and bring it to a boil over high heat while you prep.
While the water heats, finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium-high heat, then brown the beef for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with a generous pinch of salt and pepper, then simmer on low for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Salt the boiling water, cook the spaghetti 10–11 minutes until al dente, and reserve a mug of pasta water before draining. Toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold beef steams it grey instead of browning, so use a wide skillet and high heat.
Burning the garlic turns the sauce bitter, so add it only for the last 30 seconds before the tomatoes.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water for 1 minute so it coats every strand.

steps: Fill the stockpot with water and bring it to the boil over high heat while you prep.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium-high heat, then brown the beef for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer on low for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Salt the boiling water and cook the spaghetti for 9–11 minutes until al dente, then drain and toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding cold beef in the pan steams it grey instead of browning it, so use medium-high heat and let it brown before stirring.
Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter, so add it only for the last 30 seconds before the tomatoes.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch the sauce clings to, so drain it and toss it straight into the sauce.
output.tip: Save a mug of starchy pasta water before draining and loosen the sauce with a splash if it looks thick.

steps: Fill the stockpot with water and bring it to the boil over high heat while you prep.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium-high heat, then brown the beef for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Salt the boiling water, cook the spaghetti for 9–11 minutes until al dente, and save a mug of pasta water before draining.
pitfalls: Crowding cold beef into the pan steams it grey instead of browning it, so use medium-high heat and break it into small pieces.
Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter, so add it only for the last 30 seconds before the tomatoes.
Under-salted pasta water leaves the spaghetti bland, so salt it generously once it is boiling.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water so the sauce clings to every strand.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces.
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat, then cook the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Simmer the sauce uncovered for 8–10 minutes, until thick enough to hold a spoon trail.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and warm it in a toaster or dry pan. Serve straight from the skillet.
pitfalls: Watery sauce makes the eggs sink and the whites spread, so reduce it until thick before adding them.
Cooking the eggs over high heat or past 7 minutes turns the yolks hard and rubbery, so keep the heat low and take the pan off while the yolks still wobble.
Undercooked pepper stays crunchy and tastes raw against the soft sauce, so soften it fully before adding the tomatoes.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it into a well without breaking the yolk.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Fry the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook on low heat for 5–6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks wobble.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and warm or toast it. Serve straight from the skillet.
pitfalls: Watery sauce makes the eggs slide around and cook unevenly, so reduce the tomatoes until thick before adding them.
Cooking the eggs over high heat or past 6 minutes turns the yolks hard and the whites rubbery.
Undercooked pepper stays crunchy and tastes raw, so soften it fully before adding the tomatoes.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it gently into its well without breaking the yolk.

steps: Dice the onion and red bell pepper into 1cm pieces.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat, then cook the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
While the sauce simmers for 8–10 minutes, until thickened, slice the bread and warm it in a low oven if you like.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook on low heat for 5–6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
Take the skillet off the heat right away and serve with the bread.
pitfalls: Watery sauce makes the eggs slide around and cook unevenly, so simmer until it coats a spoon.
Cooking the eggs on high heat leaves rubbery whites and hard yolks, so keep the heat low and covered.
Adding the eggs to undercooked pepper leaves it crunchy, so soften it fully before the tomatoes go in.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it into the sauce without breaking the yolk.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead; whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a batter and rest it.
Rub the beef with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and seasoning, then roast at 220°C for 20 minutes. Lower to 180°C and cook 1 hour 10 minutes for medium (60°C core).
Peel and cut the potatoes into 5cm chunks, parboil for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake rough. Peel the parsnips and carrots and cut into batons.
Roast the potatoes and parsnips in hot oil at 200°C for 60 minutes, turning once; add the carrots with butter for the last 40 minutes.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the tray until smoking, pour in the batter and bake 20–25 minutes.
While the puddings bake, simmer the wine and stock with the beef juices for 10 minutes to make gravy. Steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes, then carve the beef and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so wait until they are deep golden.
Pouring batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until smoking first.
Carving the beef straight from the oven sends the juices onto the board and leaves dry slices, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Dry the parboiled potatoes in the colander for 5 minutes before roasting so the surface crisps.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge, rub with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and seasoning, and rest it for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 220°C.
Peel and cut the potatoes and parsnips, then parboil the potatoes for 8–10 minutes. Drain, shake roughly and let them steam dry.

Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C for about 60 minutes for medium (core 55–60°C). Meanwhile, heat oil in a tray for 10 minutes and roast the potatoes for 60 minutes, turning once.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and rest it for 30 minutes. Toss the parsnips and carrots with oil and add them to the oven 40 minutes before serving.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the tin until smoking, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the door.
Deglaze the roasting tin with red wine, add stock and simmer for 8–10 minutes, then strain. While it reduces, steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes and carve the beef.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door during the Yorkshire pudding bake makes them collapse, so wait until they are deep golden.
Putting batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it smokes lightly.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves it dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Roughen the edges of the parboiled potatoes in the colander and roast them in very hot fat for extra crunch.

steps: Remove the beef from the fridge 1 hour ahead, rub with oil, salt, pepper, crushed garlic and chopped herbs, then whisk the batter of flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt; rest it.
Peel and cut the potatoes into 5cm chunks; parboil for 8–10 minutes, drain, shake roughly, and peel and cut the carrots and parsnips into batons.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C and cook for about 1 hour 10 minutes, to 55°C in the centre for medium.
While the beef roasts, heat oil in a tray at 200°C, add the potatoes and roast for 60 minutes, turning once; add the carrots and parsnips with butter for the last 40 minutes.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes, then raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the tin until smoking, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the door.
While the puddings bake, simmer the wine until halved, add the stock and the beef juices, and reduce for 10 minutes; steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door during baking makes the Yorkshire puddings collapse, so wait until they are deep golden.
Pouring batter into lukewarm oil gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it smokes first.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Use the beef's resting time to bake the puddings, since the foil-covered joint stays hot while the oven is at full heat.

pitfalls: Rice cooked at the last minute leaves the curry sitting and thickening, so start the rice (rinsed until the water runs clear) at the same time as the simmer to finish together.
Cooking the chicken thigh only until browned can leave the centre underdone, so make sure the pieces reach 75°C inside by the end of the simmer.
Adding the tomatoes straight from the can without reducing them leaves a sharp, thin sauce, so uncover the pan for the last 5–10 minutes to thicken it and mellow the acidity.
output.tip: Stir a spoonful of butter or 2 tbsp of cream plus a pinch of garam masala into the finished curry to round out the flavour and give it a glossy, restaurant-style finish.

pitfalls: Rinsing nothing off the marinated chicken is fine, but overloading the pan when browning drops the heat so the thighs steam and turn grey; brown in two batches.
Adding the tomatoes straight from the can without cooking them down leaves a sharp, acidic sauce; stir and reduce them for a few minutes before covering to simmer.
Skipping the salt until the end gives a flat sauce, since tikka paste and yogurt vary widely in saltiness; taste after simmering and adjust, starting with 1/2 teaspoon.
output.tip: Stir 2 tablespoons of the remaining yogurt or a splash of cream in off the heat at the end for a silkier, milder sauce that won't split.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken straight from the marinade into a crowded pan steams it instead of browning it, so brown it in two batches over medium-high heat and wipe off excess yogurt first.
Pouring cold tomatoes onto a pan with yogurt-heavy chicken and boiling hard can split the yogurt into a grainy sauce, so keep the simmer gentle with small bubbles.
Skipping rice rinsing and a rest after cooking gives sticky, uneven grains, so rinse 300g rice until the water runs clear and rest it covered for 5 minutes off the heat.
output.tip: Start the rice as the curry begins simmering so both finish together, and stir in a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon juice at the end to lift the sauce.

pitfalls: Adding soy sauce straight onto the noodles lets them soak it up unevenly and clump, so loosen the noodles first and mix the soy sauce with 30ml of water before pouring.
Skipping the pre-soak or overcooking the rice noodles leaves them either hard or broken and mushy, so soak or boil them until just tender, 4–5 minutes, then drain well.
Crowding the pan with all the tofu at once drops the oil temperature and steams the cubes instead of crisping them, so fry in 2 batches with 1cm of oil.
output.tip: Cut the broccoli into small florets and blanch for 1 minute in the noodle water so it cooks through quickly while staying bright green.

pitfalls: Overcrowding the pan when frying the tofu steams it instead of crisping it, so fry in 2 batches with about 1cm of oil.
Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water or cooking them too long makes them clump and break up in the wok; soak in hot tap water until just pliable, then drain well.
Adding the soy sauce straight onto the tofu at the end softens the crust, so pour it around the edge of the wok and toss for no more than 30 seconds.
output.tip: Toss the pressed tofu cubes in cornstarch with a pinch of salt and pepper, then shake off the excess in a sieve so the coating fries thin and evenly golden.

pitfalls: Adding soy sauce directly to the noodles in a hot wok makes them clump and season unevenly, so loosen the noodles with a splash of water and toss the soy sauce through them first.
Overcrowding the pan when frying the tofu steams the cubes instead of crisping them, so fry in 2 batches with 1cm of oil.
Soaking the rice noodles too long or cooking them fully beforehand leaves them mushy in the wok, so soak in hot water for only 5–7 minutes until just pliable.
output.tip: Blanch the broccoli florets for 1 minute and drain them well before stir-frying, so they cook through quickly and stay bright green.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja pane need seejärel väikeses potis keema, 40–50 minutit pehmeks.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae liha suures potis kuumas rasvas igast küljest pruuniks, siis lisa sibul ja prae veel 3–4 minutit.
Lisa hapukapsas ja loorberilehed, kalla peale vähe vett ja hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1 tund, aeg-ajalt segades.
Koori kartulid, lõika tükkideks ja keeda eraldi pehmeks, 15–20 minutit, või lisa need potti viimase 25 minuti ajaks.
Sega valmis kruubid ja kartulid kapsa-lihaseguga, hauta kaane all veel 10–15 minutit ning maitsesta soolaga.
pitfalls: Ära jäta hapukapsast liiga kauaks ilma vedelikuta: põhi kõrbeb ja roog muutub kibedaks.
Ära prae liha korraga liiga palju: see hakkab hauduma, mitte pruunistuma, ja roog jääb maitsetuks.
Ära soolasta enne kapsa maitsmist: hapukapsas on juba soolane ja roog võib minna liiga soolaseks.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis tõmbavad maitsed paremini kokku.

steps: Loputa odrakruubid ja leota need külmas vees, et need hiljem kiiremini pehmeneksid.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae liha kuumas potis osade kaupa pruuniks, siis lisa sibul ja prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed, kurnatud kruubid ja nii palju vett, et see jääb napilt kattuma; keeda kaane all madalal kuumusel 1 tund.
Kooruta kartulid, lõika need 3 cm tükkideks ja lisa potti, kui ülejäänud toit on poolel teel.
Hauta veel 40–50 minutit, kuni liha ja kruubid on pehmed ning kartul laguneb veidi; sega aeg-ajalt, et põhi ei kõrbeks, ja eemalda loorberilehed.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja toit muutub ühtlaseks mänguks.
Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma segamata: kruubid ja kapsas kleepuvad põhja ning kõrbevad.
Ära lisa liiga palju vett korraga: toit jääb vesiseks, mitte paksuks ja hautatuks.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis maitsed sulavad paremini kokku.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees, kuni valmistad ülejäänu ette; nii keevad need pehmemaks.
Haki sibul ja lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks.
Prae liha potis kuuma rasva peal kõrgel kuumusel pruuniks, vajadusel kahes jaos, ja lisa sibul pooleks minutiks.
Lisa nõrutatud hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see jääb peaaegu katteks; hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 45 minutit.
Koori ja tükelda kartulid, lisa need koos nõrutatud kruupidega potti ning hauta veel 40–45 minutit, kuni kõik on pehme.
Sega aeg-ajalt, lisa vajadusel kuuma vett ja maitsesta soolaga alles lõpus, sest hapukapsas on juba soolane.
pitfalls: Ära maitsesta toitu enne lõppu soolaga: hapukapsas ja soolane liha teevad roa liiga soolaseks.
Ära jäta potti ilma jälgimata: kruubid ja kartul imavad vedeliku ning põhi kõrbeb kergesti põhja.
Ära lõika sealiha liiga väikeseks: pika haudumise ajal kuivab see ära ja laguneb.
output.tip: Kui hapukapsas on väga hapu, loputa seda enne kiiresti külma veega, siis jääb roa maitse pehmemaks.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: need ei küpse 20 minutiga läbi ja jäävad lõhe all toored.
Ära jäta kartuleid ilma õli ja soolata ahju: viilud kleepuvad plaadile kinni ja jäävad kahvatuks ning mõnuta.
Ära pane külma otse külmikust võetud lõhet kuumadele kartulitele: filee küpseb ebaühtlaselt ja välimine osa kuivab ära, enne kui keskosa valmis saab.
output.tip: Võta lõhe 15 minutit enne ahju panekut külmikust välja ja kuivata paberrätikuga, siis küpseb see ühtlasemalt ning jääb mahlane.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja lõhe on valmis, kui kartul on veel kõva.
Ära pane kartuleid ahjuplaadile kuiva ja õlita: need kleepuvad külge ja jäävad kuivaks, nii et vaja on veidi oliiviõli ja soola juba esimesel küpsetusel.
Ära küpseta lõhet 15 minutit paksu tüki kaupa ilma nahka kontrollimata: kui tükk on üle 3 cm paks, kuivab õhem ots ära enne, kui keskosa valmis saab.
output.tip: Kontrolli lõhe valmidust kahvliga: kui liha laguneb kergelt helbeteks ja keskel on see veel veidi läikiv, on kala just paraja mahlasusega, umbes 60 °C sisetemperatuuril.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksuks (üle 5 mm): 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja jäävad lõhe all toortaoliseks.
Ära pane kartuleid ahjuplaadile ilma õlita: viilud kleepuvad külge ja jäävad kahvatuks.
Ära lisa sidrunimahla kartulitele enne lõhe lisamist ega kasta kala liiga rohke mahlaga: kala heledamaks muutunud pind muutub kuivaks ja hapuks.
output.tip: Kontrolli lõhe küpsust 52–55 °C sisetemperatuuri järgi või vajuta kahvliga: liha peab kihiliselt lahti tulema, aga olema keskelt veel mahlane.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulatatud võid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna osaliselt kinni keeta ja taigen jääb tombuline.
Ära vala taigent pannile liiga paksu kihina: pannkook küpseb seest toorelt ja ei ole enam õhuke, seega kalla ainult nii palju, et põhi õhukeselt kattub.
Ära keera pannkooki liiga vara ümber: kui serv pole veel kuldne ja pind matt, rebeneb pannkook spaatli peal.
output.tip: Määri esimese pannkoogi jaoks pann kergelt võiga ja hoia kuumus keskmisena (umbes 180 °C), siis saavad ülejäänud pannkoogid ühtlaselt kuldsed ilma lisarasvata.

pitfalls: Ära vala kogu jahu korraga vedelikku: taignasse jäävad tükid, mis ei lahustu ka seisma jättes ja pannkoogid saavad kogelised.
Ära lisa sulatatud võid kuumalt: see võib muna osaliselt kinni keeta ja taigen läheb sõmeraks.
Ära jäta panni liiga kuumaks: pannkook pruunistub väljast kiiresti, aga jääb sisemuselt toorest ja rebeneb keerates.
output.tip: Määri esimese pannkoogi jaoks pann kergelt võiga ja kuumuta keskmisel-kõrgel kuumusel (umbes 180 °C), siis saad õhukese ja ühtlaselt kuldse pannkoogi, ning järgmistel pole enam rasva vaja.

pitfalls: Ära vala kogu jahu korraga vedelikku: tainasse jäävad tükid, mida hiljem on raske välja vispeldada.
Ära pane sulavõid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna osaliselt kinni keeta ja tekitada taignas helbeid.
Ära küpseta liiga kuuma pannil ega keera pannkooki enne aegsasti: serv kõrbeb, keskosa jääb toorEKS ja pannkook rebeneb.
output.tip: Määri pann enne esimest pannkooki õhukeselt võiga ja küpseta iga pannkoogi esimene pool 1–2 minutit 180–200 °C juures, kuni pind on matt ja serv kuldne, siis on keeramine lihtne.
